about: Channels outside the Ukraine war: Middle East, Iran, Asia, Africa, cyber and markets.
Verified the same way as the war channels, on 16 September 2026. Telegram's coverage is
very uneven outside the Russian-speaking world: this file is short because most of the
obvious candidates either publish no public channel preview or had gone silent, and the
gaps are listed in ``docs/TELEGRAM_CHANNEL_COVERAGE.md`` rather than filled with an

channels.name: Israel Defense Forces
channels.reason: The Israeli military's own statements on strikes, operations and casualties, issued by a belligerent about its own operations.

channels.name: Israel War Room
channels.operator: Israel War Room, an Israeli advocacy media project
channels.reason: Fast pro-Israel aggregation of strike and security claims; openly campaigning rather than reporting.

channels.name: Quds News Network
channels.operator: Quds News Network, a Palestinian media network
channels.reason: Palestinian coverage of raids, strikes and casualties in Gaza and the West Bank, from the other side of the same events.

channels.name: Press TV
channels.operator: Press TV, the English channel of Iranian state broadcaster IRIB
channels.reason: Iranian state broadcasting in English; the Iranian government's framing of regional strikes, nuclear talks and sanctions.

channels.name: IRNA
channels.operator: Islamic Republic News Agency, the Iranian state news agency
channels.reason: Iran's state wire in Persian, carrying official announcements before their English translations appear.

channels.name: South China Morning Post
channels.operator: South China Morning Post, Hong Kong, owned by Alibaba Group
channels.reason: The most consistent English coverage of China, Hong Kong and Taiwan tensions available on Telegram; ownership and jurisdiction are a constraint on it.

channels.name: Mali Actu
channels.operator: Mali Actu (maliactu.net), a Malian news outlet
channels.reason: Malian outlet covering the Sahel insurgency, junta politics and Russian paramilitary activity; posts in bursts rather than daily.

channels.name: OSINTdefender
channels.reason: High-tempo English aggregation of conflict claims worldwide; frequently first, and its early claims are often corrected afterwards.

channels.name: Bloomberg
channels.reason: Markets, sanctions and energy headlines; the financial read on events the conflict channels cover first.

channels.name: vx-underground
channels.reason: Ransomware group activity, leaks and malware research, usually posted here before it reaches vendor blogs.

channels.name: The Hacker News
channels.reason: Established security news outlet; vulnerability and intrusion coverage in step with vendor advisories.

channels.name: BleepingComputer
channels.reason: Incident and ransomware reporting with technical detail, and the usual first confirmation of a named victim organisation.

channels.name: RedPacket Security
channels.reason: Automated aggregation of advisories, breach claims and leak-site listings; volume rather than judgement.
